How often does each OPDI item exist, and when it does, how close is it to
an independent record? The figures come from three days processed worldwide
with the current methods.

## Two measures: availability and accuracy

They are kept apart and never merged into one figure: an item can be
available and wrong, or rare and exact. **Found is not the same as correct.**

**Availability** is how often an item exists, measured in two ways.

- *Among OPDI's own flights.* Of the flights in OPDI's flight list that
  could carry the item, the share that do. A departure item (take-off time,
  off-block time, line-up, ...) counts among the flights with a departure
  airport, an arrival item among those with a destination airport, the
  other items among all flights. It needs no reference, so it is given for
  every item and every airport in the world.
- *Against a reference.* Of the movements in an independent record, the
  share for which OPDI has the item. It also counts flights OPDI did not
  receive at all, so it is the better measure of what a study will miss
  where a reference exists.

**Accuracy** is how close the item is to the reference when both exist. For
a time, it is the share of OPDI's times within 60 s of the recorded time,
with the median and the 90th percentile of the difference. For an airport,
runway, stand or aircraft type, it is the share equal to the record. For the
distance flown, it is the share within 10 % of the route length that Network
Manager records.

## How to read the labels

Every share has a label beside it. The labels are words, so tables can be
searched for them; they never replace the number.

| Measure | Label | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Availability | high | at least 80 % |
| | partial | 50 % to under 80 % |
| | low | under 50 % |
| Accuracy | good | at least 80 % of the compared values agree (rules above) |
| | fair | 50 % to under 80 % |
| | limited | under 50 % |
| | too few compared | the reference has at least 30 movements, but fewer than 30 OPDI values could be compared: the item is mostly missing, read its availability |
| | no reference | no reference, or fewer than 30 reference movements |

: The labels. {.striped}

A label is computed over the count beside it: a figure built on a few dozen
movements is less certain than one built on thousands, whatever the label.

## In brief

- **Take-off and landing times** are the most reliable times. At the
  European airports that send airport records,
  80.8 % of the recorded take-offs and
  81.7 % of the recorded landings have an OPDI time,
  and 93.2 % and 94.5 % of those times are
  within 60 s of the record.
- **Block times** are limited by reception on the ground. Only
  35.0 % of the recorded off-blocks and
  33.4 % of the recorded in-blocks have an OPDI time;
  40.3 % of the off-block times and
  72.0 % of the in-block times are within 60 s.
- **Departure and destination airports, runways and aircraft type** agree
  with the records in most cases where they exist; the destination airport
  is missing more often than the departure airport
  ([why](../limitations.qmd#lim-airports)).
- **Distance circle crossings** at 40 and 100 NM are close to the records:
  most of them within a few seconds.
- **Events in the air with no reference** (tops of climb and descent, level
  segments, flight-level and FIR crossings, holds, point merge) are given
  with their availability only.

## Every item

{{< include _generated/overall_lookup.md >}}

Counts are given to four significant figures.

- `ATOT` and `ALDT` have two rows: against the airport records at the
  airports that send them, and against Network Manager at the other
  European airports.
- The rows with `info.method` show the two methods that produce these times
  separately.
- The runway and stand rows have no availability of their own among OPDI's
  flights; read the row of the event that names them.

## What OPDI is compared with

- **Airport records.** The movement records that airport operators send to
  EUROCONTROL: off-block, take-off, landing and in-block times, runway, stand,
  and the times at which the flight crossed the 40 NM and 100 NM circles
  around the airport. Of the 100 busiest European airports, 72 send them.
  Many round times to the whole minute, so differences under about half a
  minute cannot be judged; labels use 60 s.
- **Network Manager records.** EUROCONTROL's records of every flight in or
  through European airspace: departure and destination airport, aircraft
  type, route length, and a take-off and landing time. Its take-off time is
  the off-block time plus a taxi time, so its times are estimates. They are
  used for times only at European airports that send no airport records.
- **No reference.** For many items nothing exists to compare with (no
  record gives a top of climb or a holding pattern), and outside Europe
  there are no airport records at all; Network Manager knows only the flights
  to and from Europe there. These items get availability among OPDI's own
  flights only.

Records are matched to the nearest OPDI flight within 6 hours by aircraft
address (the transponder's 24-bit code), call sign and airport. Records
without an address are not matched or counted. A movement whose flight
belongs to the previous day (for example a landing just after midnight)
counts as not found, so availability against a reference is slightly low at
each day's ends.

## The three days

Wednesday 10 June, Sunday 14 June and Wednesday 17 June 2026, processed
worldwide from the OpenSky archive with the current pipeline settings.
Three days rather than one give smaller airports enough movements to be
scored; the figures cover the three days together, and airport records exist
for all three.

## What this means for your study

- **Taxi-out and taxi-in times** need a block time and a runway time of the
  same flight, and off-block times are often late. Restrict a taxi-time
  study to airports labelled good or fair for
  [off-block](airports.qmd#off-block) (or in-block) and report how many
  flights remain. Where no receiver hears aircraft on the ground, block
  times are missing, not wrong: see
  [where ground events are nearly absent](airports.qmd#ground-reception).
- **Runway times and runway use** can be studied at most European airports
  that send records. Separate the two methods with `info.method` when
  comparing airports: they have different errors.
- **Arrival flows at 40 and 100 NM** (for example additional time in the
  terminal area) can use the circle crossings; they are close to the
  records.
- **Outside Europe**, a high availability says the item exists, not that it
  is right.
- **Events with no reference** suit comparisons between airports, days or
  airlines computed the same way, but no figure says how close they are to
  the truth.
